body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 17, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high of 99° and air quality at moderate. Overnight, a group of juveniles brandishing a firearm on Monterey Street was the headline call of the night. Today’s top story: the trial begins in a 2019 Bakersfield homicide case that KGET 17 reports stemmed from an argument over alleged “rude comments.” Let’s get caught up on the night, the weather, and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night belonged to a couple of gun calls — the juvenile-brandishing incident on Monterey Street and a shots-fired report that had officers checking emergency rooms — but it was a busy one overall. Around 11 p.m., a caller reported a group of five juveniles — one of whom pointed a firearm at them after claiming a gang affiliation — on Monterey Street. All were described as wearing dark clothing. No shots were reported on the air, and units were responding as the feed moved on. Shortly before 9:40 p.m., a possible shots-fired incident had units checking local hospitals for gunshot victims and looking for a suspect vehicle. The exact location was unclear on the air. At 9:54 p.m., a domestic violence call in progress (273.6) drew multiple units to a residence on Animas Court. Just after 10:30 p.m., crews found a one-acre grass fire with a slow rate of spread near the bike path, accessing it from Oak Street and pulling an additional line. Around 11:03 p.m., an ex-boyfriend reportedly smashed a vehicle windshield with a shotgun in the FoodMaxx parking lot on Ming Avenue. The reporting party was standing by. At 11:33 p.m., a possible burglary at a Manhattan Drive residence — a sliding back door found shattered — had deputies investigating. The log also noted a vehicle fire inside a tow yard; an alarm at the AutoZone on Ming Avenue; a reckless driver on southbound I-5 north of Lebec; medical aids at the Pacific Palms Apartments on O Street, at a residence on Covey Avenue, and at the Bank of America on Coffee Road; a verbal disturbance in the Baker Street area; a small fire on the riverbed at Yokuts Park; and a welfare check at Applecreek Court involving a young child.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 99° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 81° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 59 — moderate.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** the trial begins today in a 2019 Bakersfield homicide case that stemmed from an argument over alleged “rude comments.” The case, which dates back to 2019, centers on an altercation that escalated to violence. The station notes the unusual circumstances of the incident, which prosecutors argue began with a dispute over perceived disrespect. The trial is expected to draw attention to how everyday conflicts can turn deadly in our community.

**According to 23ABC,** Robert F. Kennedy Jr. toured a Bakersfield program last week that he believes could reshape how schools teach children about food and nutrition. Kennedy visited Edible Schoolyard Kern County, a program that brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum. Students grow their own food in school gardens, then use that fresh produce in kitchen lessons. The goal is to connect what students learn in the classroom to what ends up on their plates. Congressman Vince Fong said the hands-on approach is what makes the program unique and why he believes it could be expanded. Kennedy pointed to the program’s focus on fresh food, including school cafeterias he said are buying fresh produce, as an example of how schools can change the way children eat without spending more money.

**KGET 17 also tells us that** actor Hayden Panettiere, who starred in “Heroes” and “Nashville,” has died at the age of 36. Panettiere was known for her roles in several popular television series and films. Her passing has prompted an outpouring of tributes from fans and colleagues across the entertainment industry.

## Something good

Robert F. Kennedy Jr. tours Bakersfield program he says could reshape how schools teach kids about food. The program aims to transform education around food in schools. 

## Coming up this week

This week brings several public meetings and events worth noting. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m. The Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4:00 p.m. the same day. Also on Tuesday, the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10:00 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. And at the Fox Theater, the entertainment lineup includes Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22; Rodney Carrington on August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28; Willie Barcena on August 29; Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29; and MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA on September 4.
